# Ship post-release branch cleanup fails non-deterministically (shared /tmp report path / concurrent agents)

## Problem statement

The ship skill's post-release branch cleanup (`runPostReleaseCleanup` in
`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`) fails non-deterministically in a
multi-agent (herdr) environment because it reads and writes a **fixed shared
temp path** (`${os.tmpdir()}/cleanup-summary.json`): when two release/cleanup
processes run concurrently, one clobbers the other's report, so the run logs
"Failed to read summarize report; skipping local cleanup.", then silently
reports "Found 0 merged local branch(es)" and "Pruned 0 local branch(es)" as
if the repository were clean, and the follow-on remote prune also fails.
Observed during the AI_Hell v0.1.10 dev→main release; the same scripts succeed
when re-run standalone.

## Users

- **Agents (Map / herdr):** run automated releases and must not be misled by a
  false "clean" cleanup results.
- **Operators:** trust that post-release cleanup either happened or produced an
  actionable, non-silent warning.
- **Other projects consuming the shared ship/cleanup skills** (AI_Hell, etc.):
  any project can hit the race when releases coincide.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-release cleanup uses a **unique temp path per run** (e.g. derived from
   `mkdtempSync`) for the summarize report; a unit test with two
   concurrent-invocation fakes proves no shared-path clobber.
2. A failed `summarize_branches.py` run or report read no longer silently
   reports "0 merged branches" as if the repo were clean — it logs a distinct,
   actionable warning naming the deterministic remediation (unique temp path).
3. The cleanup stays **non-blocking**: a cleanup failure never changes the
   release exit code (existing AC3 preserved).
4. A transient failure (summarize run / report read / remote prune) is
   **retried once** before the actionable warning is emitted.

## Constraints

- Fix must live in the **SorraAgents** repo (ship/cleanup skills are symlinked
  from `~/.pi/agent/skills` into `SorraAgents/skill/`); AI_Hell does not vendor
  these files.
- Cleanup scripts' standalone behaviour (`summarize_branches.py`,
  `prune_local_branches.py`, `delete_remote_branches.py`) must not change.
- Non-blocking guarantee must be preserved (existing AC3 of
  SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG).
- Tests run under `node --test "tests/unit/**/*.mjs"` in SorraAgents.

## Existing state

`runPostReleaseCleanup` passes a fixed `${tempDir}/cleanup-summary.json` to
`summarize_branches.py --report` (~L1110) and reads it back (~L1135). On read
failure it sets `reportData = { branches: [] }` and logs only the generic
"skipping local cleanup" warning, then proceeds to report "Found 0 merged local
branch(es)". The branches-to-delete file already uses `mkdtempSync`
(`cleanup-branches-*`), so only the report path is shared.

## Desired change

- Derive a unique report path per run (mkdtemp-based) used for both the
  `--report` argument and the read-back, so concurrent runs cannot clobber.
- Distinguish a real "no merged branches" result from a failed enumerate/read:
  log an actionable warning (unique-path remediation) instead of the misleading
  "0 merged branches".
- Add a single retry with small backoff for the transient step(s) before
  emitting the warning, preserving non-blocking behaviour.
- Extend `tests/unit/test-run-release-cleanup.mjs` with the concurrency-clobber
  test and report-failure-warning test.

## Key Files:

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `runPostReleaseCleanup` (report path
  L1110/L1135, retry logic, warning text)
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-cleanup.mjs` — new AC1 concurrency fake test,
  AC2 warning test, AC4 retry test

## Risks & assumptions

- **Retry must not mask real errors** — the single retry is for transient
  failures only; the actionable warning must still be emitted on the second
  failure (assumption: failures are quiet enough to retry once without
  doubling wall-clock time; mitigation: small backoff).
- **Scope creep** — deeper cleanup-skill refactoring, branch-deletion policy
  changes, or fixing `delete_remote_branches.py`/`summarize_branches.py`
  behaviour are out of scope; if such work is discovered, record it as new
  linked work items (not here).
- **Test isolation** — the concurrency test must not touch the real
  `/tmp/cleanup-summary.json` or run real git commands; fakes only
  (assumption: existing `setupRunReleaseFixture` harness is reused/adapted).
- **Cross-repo tracking** — item originated in the AI_Hell worklog
  (AH-0MUZGWL14001E1EU, moved here per producer decision Q1c); AI_Hell leaves
  no orphan reference after deletion.
- **Non-blocking guarantee** — AC3 must survive the retry addition; the retry
  must also be non-blocking.

## Related work

- SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG — Automate post-release cleanup (introduced this code).
- AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ — Discord notification fails (precedent: ship-skill bug
  tracked in AH worklog, fixed in SorraAgents).
- SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH — Live-repo guard concurrency (related concurrency issue).
- SA-0MUJQ5BPF001PICU — Test-suite flakiness under concurrent agent load.
- discovered-from: AH-0MUZGWL14001E1EU (moved from AI_Hell worklog);
  discovered-from: release-v0.1.10.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should the fix be implemented/tracked? The code lives in
  SorraAgents (ship/cleanup skills); this item is tracked in the AI_Hell
  worklog." — Answer (producer): **(c)** "check an equivalent doesn't already
  exist first, delete this item" (i.e. move the item entirely to SorraAgents).
  Source: interactive reply. Research: searched the SorraAgents worklog for
  `cleanup-summary`, `runPostReleaseCleanup`, `post-release cleanup`, `tmp
  path`, `shared report`, `concurrent agents`, `branch cleanup` — no equivalent
  open/closed item; only the completed feature SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG and two
  unrelated concurrency items. Outcome: created SA-0MV6JQP9K004QGUT here and
  deleted AH-0MUZGWL14001E1EU.
- Q2: "Is 'retry once' in scope? Expected Behaviour promises it but the ACs do
  not require it." — Answer (producer): **(a)** add it as AC4. Source:
  interactive reply.

## Goal

`_git_commit_evidence` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` resolves a
stranded child's pushed-commit evidence with
`git log <ref> --grep <child_id> -n 1`. `--grep` matches the **whole commit

SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 timed out after 3600 s with its own commit (`9119e4117`)
still unpushed in its worktree, and `drive` reported it as *stranded* with

whose body names SA-0MVX359B7008R9F3 as the future home of the detection
module. The verdict told the operator to `--finalise-stranded` a child whose
work had never been pushed.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Commit evidence matches only commits whose **subject** references the
   work-item id, never a body-only mention.
2. A regression test pins the false-positive: a commit whose body mentions
   another item's id is not evidence for that item.
3. A driven child whose commit is still only in its own worktree is reported

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_git_commit_evidence`

## Objective

Make `/skill:ship release` judge the importance of the work items in the release and propose the semantically correct semver bump (patch, minor, or major), instead of always bumping patch — with the producer asked in the PI session before any non-patch bump is applied.

## Problem Statement

The ship skill currently always increments the `z` (patch) component of the release version (`merge-dev-to-main.sh` defaults `BUMP="patch"`), even when the release adds new or breaking capability. Releases that add features therefore ship as patch versions (e.g. `v0.1.19` instead of `v0.2.0`), misrepresenting the release's impact and forcing the producer to remember `--bump minor` manually.

## Users

- **Release manager (the PI agent running `/skill:ship release`)** — must judge the release's importance from the items being shipped and propose the right bump without extra flags.
- **Producer** — must see and approve any non-patch bump, in the session, with a full justification naming the items that triggered it.

Example user stories:

- As a release manager, when every item in the release is a fix, chore, or documentation change, I want the release to bump patch automatically so that I don't have to think about semver.
- As a release manager, when the release contains meaningful new capability, I want to propose a minor bump with evidence, rather than silently shipping it as a patch.
- As a producer, I want to be asked, in the session, before a minor or major bump is applied, with a justification naming the items and why they warrant the bump — and I want to be able to decline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ship skill's release workflow gains a startup **version-bump evaluation** step that runs before any git mutation and gathers every release candidate (`wl list --stage in_review`) with enough context for a judgement: ID, title, type, priority, `## Impact`/user story and a short description excerpt.
- The agent judges the importance of the release from those items and proposes exactly one bump: **patch** when the release only fixes, documents, or maintains; **minor** when it adds meaningful new capability; **major** when it breaks or removes existing capability or otherwise changes behaviour incompatibly (the existing `--bump` override remains available).
- A **patch** proposal proceeds automatically with no producer interaction — the current `--bump patch` behaviour and `merge-dev-to-main.sh` default are unchanged.
- A **minor or major** proposal prints a full justification — each contributing item ID and title, why it warrants the bump, and the proposed `old → new` version — and the agent asks the producer **in the PI session**; no git mutation, tag, PR, or worklog close occurs until the producer approves.
- Producer approval proceeds with the approved `--bump`; a declined non-patch proposal is honoured (the agent does not apply it, and records the decision and the producer's preferred bump in the session and on the release's work item).
- In a non-interactive/headless context where the producer cannot be asked, a minor or major proposal is never auto-approved: the agent records the justification, flags the item for producer review, and stops.
- The judgement is based on the release items' content (Impact/description/capability), not on `issueType` or a label lookup; the justification cites the evidence used.
- Minor bumps reset `z` to `0`, and major bumps reset `y` and `z` to `0`, reusing the existing `release/bump-version.js` semantics rather than duplicating version arithmetic.
- Unit tests cover: candidate gathering (including an empty candidate set), the review packet/justification rendering, patch auto-proceed, and the non-patch approval-pending behaviour (no mutation); no test reads or mutates the live worklog.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, and code comments.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Releases that add or break capability will carry a version number that reflects it, and producers will be asked in-session to approve that call with evidence instead of policing `--bump` flags by hand.

## Existing State

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` sets `BUMP="patch"` by default and accepts `--bump patch|minor|major` (already validates the value).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` parses and forwards `--bump` to the merge script; the wrapper has no bump evaluation step and its documented exit codes are `0`–`14`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` already implements `patch`/`minor`/`major` arithmetic correctly (including `z = 0` on minor and `y = z = 0` on major) and resolves `package.json` or `pyproject.toml` as the version source.
- Release candidates are items with `stage: in_review` (`check-audit-gate.js::getCandidateItems`), so the candidate set already exists.
- The release wrapper subprocess is non-interactive, but the ship skill itself is a PI skill executed by an agent in a session — the agent, not the shell script, is the component that can ask the producer.

## Desired Change

1. Add a small, unit-testable helper (e.g. `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js`) that gathers release candidates and renders a compact review packet: per item `id`, `title`, `issueType`, `priority`, `## Impact` (or user story) and a truncated description excerpt, plus the current version and the three candidate bump outcomes. It gathers and renders only — no judgement, no mutation.
2. Add a "Version bump evaluation" step at the start of the documented release workflow in `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (before gates and merge): run the preflight, judge the release's importance, and choose patch/minor/major.
3. Patch → run the release normally (patch is the existing default).
4. Minor/major → present the justification to the producer in the session and wait for approval; on approval run `run-release.js --bump <approved>`; on decline, do not apply.
5. Keep the judgement rationale and the producer's decision in the session output and, where the release is tied to a work item, in a comment so the version choice is auditable.
6. Update `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and the SKILL.md workflow/argument docs to describe the evaluation step and the in-session approval gate.

## Constraints

- **Judgement stays with the agent:** no issue-type or label mapping, and no mechanical classifier is added — the evaluation prompt/rubric is documented, and the agent makes the call from the items' content.
- **Producer gates non-patch bumps:** minor and major bumps must never be applied without an explicit producer approval in the session. Patch bumps stay automatic.
- **Fail-closed in headless runs:** where no producer is available (downtime/automated dispatches), a minor/major proposal must stop with producer review rather than self-approve.
- **Backward compatible:** an explicit `--bump` keeps its current meaning and precedence; invoking `merge-dev-to-main.sh` directly keeps its `patch` default.
- **No duplicated version arithmetic:** reuse `bump-version.js` for the actual bump; the new code only gathers evidence and renders the proposal.
- **Fail-safe:** an unreadable/empty candidate set must default to patch with a warning and must never block a release that would otherwise succeed; a preflight failure must not mutate the repository.
- **No live-worklog test access:** unit tests must inject the candidate-fetch boundary.
- **Auditability:** the proposed and approved bump, the justification, and the producer's decision are recorded (session output plus a work-item comment for item-linked releases).

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — new "Version bump evaluation" workflow step, in-session approval gate, argument/behaviour docs.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` — new candidate-gathering/review-packet helper (and its tests).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — unchanged `--bump` forwarding, plus any logging of the decided bump; verify no new git side effects.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — receives the decided `--bump`; default unchanged.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` — reused as-is for arithmetic (verify minor resets patch to `0`, major resets minor and patch).
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `getCandidateItems` is the release-candidate source.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — reference for the evaluation step and approval gate.
- `skill/ship/tests/` — new unit tests for the preflight helper and the approval-pending path.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** — Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (introduced the bump step and `v<semver>` tag convention).
- **SA-0MVN2B0DJ00135W0** — ship: bump-version.js must support Python projects (version source resolution).
- **SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM** — Fix bump-version.js REPO_ROOT resolution for global skill installs.
- **SA-0MQI6MDUP001S8NL** — bump-version.js isMainModule check fails on symlinked install paths.
- **SA-0MRGVN9XM003LNQ7** — Close work items when shipping (uses the released version in `Shipped in v<version>` markers).
- **SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR** — Newly-created-tag gate (precedent for a fail-closed startup gate with a distinct exit code).
- **SA-0MUIVIJFT0009ZNV** — Missing-script fail-fast (precedent for refusing early, before any git/worklog side effects).

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Judgement subjectivity (risk):** "meaningful new capability" is a judgement call, and two agents could judge the same release differently. Mitigation: a documented rubric (new capability → minor, breaking change → major, fixes/docs/maintenance only → patch), the evidence-based justification, and the producer's in-session approval for every non-patch bump.
- **Producer availability (risk):** a headless release cannot ask anyone. Mitigation: a non-patch proposal in a headless run stops with producer review instead of self-approving; patch releases are unaffected.
- **Agent discipline (risk):** the gate lives in the documented workflow, so a release run by bypassing the skill (direct `run-release.js`) is not gated. Mitigation: document the workflow as the canonical path, and keep the version arithmetic and safety gates in the script unchanged.
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-item bump annotations, automatic CHANGELOG grouping, and mechanical classification are separate opportunities and should be filed as follow-up items rather than folded into this change.
- **Empty candidate set:** a release with no `in_review` items (e.g. hotfix) defaults to patch and logs why.
- **`--skip-checks` interaction (assumption):** `--skip-checks` bypasses branch/critical gates only; the bump evaluation still runs, and an explicit `--bump` remains an operator override.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (basis for minor-worthiness):** How should the release's importance be judged?
  - Options considered: (A) by `issueType`; (B) by `priority`; (C) by an explicit label/tag; (D) the agent's interpretation of the items' importance.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "It's not about issue type or label. It's about your interpretation of the importance of the items in the release. Make the best call you can. Check with the producer." → **Option D**, with a documented rubric and producer confirmation.
- **Q2 (approval mechanism):** How is the producer asked to approve a proposed minor/major bump?
  - Options considered: (A) fail-closed exit code + producer re-runs with `--bump`; (B) an interactive prompt inside the PI session; (C) automatic bump with a warning.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "It's a skill in PI, ask in the session." → **Option B**: the agent presents the justification and asks the producer in the session; the subprocess itself stays non-interactive.
- **Q3 (major inference):** Should a `major` (x) bump be inferred?
  - Options considered: (A) no — only minor/patch; (B) infer and suggest major, but never apply without producer approval.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "You can infer it and suggest it, but never implement without checking with the producer." → **Option B**: major may be proposed and justified, gated by the same in-session producer approval as minor.

# Slot-wait measurement harness counts a read of a fixture file as genuine runs (spurious 999.0 s sample)

Discovered-from: **SA-0MWATUPEW007OBIU** (residual post-fix slot-wait re-measurement follow-up).

## Problem statement

The `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` harness's genuine-run filter admits tool results from non-bash tools (e.g. `read`) when their text contains structural markers, so fixture text echoed by a file read is parsed as genuine slot-wait measurements — producing a spurious 999.0 s sample that fails the `no_run_over_120s` threshold.

## Target outcome

Fix the `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` false positive so that reading a fixture/source file can never be counted as a genuine test-slot run, restoring a trustworthy `no_run_over_120s` verdict.

## Users

- **Producer / agent operators** running the slot-wait re-measurement harness to verify the 2026-10-31 fast-lane fix removed test-slot starvation. A false-positive breach invalidates their verdict and blocks RCA closure.
- Example user story: *As a producer closing the slot-starvation RCA (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV), I need the harness verdict to reflect only real runs, so that a `fail` genuinely means users are still waiting > 120 s for a slot.*

## Existing state (evidence, 2026-11-10)

Running `python3 scripts/measure_slot_wait.py --json` over the full window reports a spurious **999.0 s** `dev_push_gate` sample. It is an artefact, not a run:

- An agent `read` `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` (session record `2026-11-10T15:23:02.987Z`).
- That file contains the fixture text `"slot_wait_seconds": 999.0` plus a `run_tests: gate-subject` marker.
- The harness's genuine-run filter trusts a tool result whose text carries a structural marker when no bash command is resolvable. A `read` tool result has no bash command, so the fixture text is parsed as **four fake gate samples** (122.687, 9.0, 1.25, 999.0).
- Effect: `dev_push_gate` inflates from 5 calls / max 0.002 s to 9 calls / max 999.0 s, and `no_run_over_120s` fails on a non-existent run.

Reproduction (confirmed): `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'scripts'); import measure_slot_wait as m; print(m.parse_block(open('tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py').read())['gate'])"` — prints the four injected samples.

Root cause: `measure()` pairs each `toolResult` with its assistant `toolCall` command via `_commands_by_tool_call`, which maps **only `bash` tool calls**. A `read`/`edit`/`write`/`grep` result therefore resolves to `command=None` and falls through to the `_has_structural_marker` fallback intended for genuine bash runs whose call record is missing (forked/compacted logs).

## Desired change

Distinguish "no command resolvable because the log is incomplete" from "no command because the result came from a non-bash tool". The `toolResult` message itself carries `toolName`; only `bash` results (or a result with no tool name) may use the structural-marker fallback. A result whose `toolName` is a non-bash tool is never a measurement, regardless of its text.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `read` (or any non-bash tool) result that merely echoes fixture text is never counted as a genuine run sample.
2. A regression test proves reading `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` (and a generic fixture file) injects zero samples.
3. The genuine-run filter still accepts real run sources (`run_tests.py`, `implement.py`, `git push`, `wait_for_job.py`) and genuine structural-marker results with no resolvable command.
4. `python3 scripts/measure_slot_wait.py --json` over the full window no longer reports the 999.0 s sample.
5. Testing/validation criterion: the regression test fails before the change and passes after it, executed through the test skill.
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The slot-wait re-measurement harness stops reporting phantom breaches, so the parent RCA's threshold verdict is trustworthy.

## Constraints

- Read-only measurement tooling; never synthesise load.
- No change to the lane ceilings or threshold values.

## Key Files

- `scripts/measure_slot_wait.py` — genuine-run filter in `measure()`; also the module docstring's "Attribution — genuine run filter" section.
- `tests/test_measure_slot_wait.py` — regression test for the fixture-echo false positive.
- `docs/dev/test-skill-reference.md` — "Genuine-run filter" paragraph (needs the bash-only rule stated).

## Related work

- `SA-0MWATUPEW007OBIU` — the follow-up item whose re-measurement surfaced this artefact.
- `SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K` — the harness's originating item.
- `SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV` — parent; its AC3 threshold check is the consumer of this verdict.
- `SA-0MWB1AZK8004VMSI` — ruff ISC004 flagging `measure_slot_wait.py`; same file, unrelated lint false-positive, do not conflate with this fix.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk**: the fix must not tighten acceptance for valid cases — genuine structural-marker results from bash runs with missing call records must still pass.
- **Confirmed assumption**: `toolResult` messages carry a `toolName` field set to `"bash"` on genuine bash tool results. Verified across a ~3,000-result sample of `~/.pi/agent/sessions`: `bash` 2346, `read` 394, `edit` 251, `write` 56, `grep` 17, `skill_path` 1 — every genuine run source is `bash`, so a `toolName != "bash"` guard is safe.
- **Assumption**: no non-bash tool legitimately carries slot-wait data in its result text.
- **Scope-creep risk**: do not extend the fix to other measurement harnesses (`measure_audit_performance.py`) unless they exhibit the same pattern.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No questions asked — the work item description provides sufficient evidence, reproduction steps, and acceptance criteria to proceed. Verified independently: (a) the reproduction prints the four injected gate samples; (b) `toolName` is present and `bash`-only for genuine runs across the session corpus; (c) the "Genuine-run filter" docs paragraph is the only prose describing the fallback.

# Remote-observed push verdict in finish

Parent: **SA-0MUOOXH17004ZEFX** — `implement.py finish` reports `git push to dev failed` when the push actually landed.

Builds on the test-first slice (the hermetic baselines land first; this slice makes them pass
and removes their `xfail(strict=True)` markers).

## Goal

As an implementation agent, when the push command is killed at the timeout but `origin/dev`
already points at my commit, I want `finish` to record the completion comment and leave the
item `completed`/`in_review` instead of resetting it to `open`; and as the producer, when
`finish` does report a push failure I want the report to say whether the commit was verified
**absent** from `origin/dev` or whether verification itself could not run, so I know exactly
what recovery is needed.

## Context

`git_push_to_dev()` (`implement.py` L5629) spawns `git push origin <branch>:refs/heads/dev` in
its own process group. On `TimeoutExpired` it process-group-kills the push and raises
`PushTimeoutError` (L4667); on a non-zero exit it raises `PushNonFastForwardError` for
non-fast-forward wording, otherwise logs `git push to dev failed` and returns `False`. There is
no post-failure remote check. `phase_finish()` Step 6 (L12011) maps a `False` return to
`RuntimeError("git push to dev failed.")`, posts a manual-push comment on `PushTimeoutError`,
and the outer `RuntimeError` handler resets the status to `open`; steps 6a–8 (post-push
ancestry assertion, cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync) and the
`StatusLifecycle(target_stage="in_review")` exit run only after a successful push.
`_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050) retries the push inside the worktree and has the
same false-failure exposure.

## Desired change

1. Add `_verify_commit_on_remote(cwd, commit_hash, timeout=...) -> bool | None`: resolve the
   full hash, read `origin`'s `refs/heads/dev` tip (`git ls-remote`), fetch that ref when the
   tip differs (bounded), and return `True` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor` says the commit
   is reachable, `False` when positively absent, `None` when the probe itself failed
   (network/auth/timeout).
2. Route every non-success push outcome through that probe. Recommended shape: have
   `git_push_to_dev()` raise a distinct "interrupted but verified landed" signal (or return an
   outcome object) rather than `False`/`PushTimeoutError`, so `phase_finish` can mark
   `steps.push.verified_after_failure`, comment, and continue on the success path;
   `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` handles the same signal on its retry.
3. Keep the conservative failure paths unchanged (`open`, manual-push comment, worktree
   retained) with the unknown-outcome wording when the probe returns `None`.
4. Extract the probe so the existing post-*success* ancestry assertion
   `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084, SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U, now completed) reuses it
   rather than shipping a second divergent probe; note the reuse on both items.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_push_to_dev()` (L5629), `PushTimeoutError` (L4667), `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` (L11050), `phase_finish()` Step 6 (L12011), `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (L8084); new `_verify_commit_on_remote()` helper.
- `tests/test_implement_push_landed_detection.py` — the baselines from the test-first slice.
- `tests/test_implement_push_timeout.py` — interrupted-push coverage.
- `tests/test_implement_non_fast_forward_recovery.py` — retry-push path.
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_no_diff_status.py` — the annotation noting the fake must keep resolving a published commit.

## Constraints

- **Positive verification only.** Never report success for a commit that was not observed on `origin/dev`; do not weaken the terminal-status read-back guarantee (OSL-0MVME1PI5005WU58).
- **No pre-push hook on verification.** The hook runs the full suite (~minutes); verification uses `ls-remote`/`fetch`/`merge-base` only and is bounded (recommended ~60 s). A verification fetch updates only remote-tracking refs, which the live-repo guard already excludes.
- **Ancestry, not equality.** Sibling sessions may push after ours; the commit is landed when it is an *ancestor* of the current `origin/dev` tip. Resolve the short hash from `git_get_commit_hash()` to a full hash before the ancestry check.
- **No force-push, no history rewrite, no `reset --hard`** of the shared main checkout; recovery stays additive.
- **Preserve existing behaviour:** non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry (WL-0MUYTCF4L000FX3M), worktree retention on genuine failure (WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1), pre-push main-checkout mutation guard, and `_sync_parent_branch` safe-skip semantics.
- **Report fields are additive.** `steps.push` keeps its existing `success`/`hash` keys (a cleanup test indexes the literal push step); the verified-landed marker is a new optional key, never a renamed or repurposed one.
- **No workflow-language change:** only which outcome (success vs failure) `finish` selects when the remote says the commit landed.
- **Source of truth:** the fix lands in this repository's `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`; the installed copy at `~/.pi/agent/skills/implement/` picks it up only after `scripts/install_pi.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Single shared remote-verification probe.** A new `_verify_commit_on_remote(cwd, commit_hash, timeout) -> bool | None` helper in `implement.py` resolves the full hash (resolving the short hash returned by `git_get_commit_hash()`), reads `origin`'s `refs/heads/dev` tip (`git ls-remote`), fetches that ref when the tip differs (bounded, ~60 s), and returns `True` when `git merge-base --is-ancestor <full-hash> <remote-tip>` reports the commit reachable, `False` when positively absent, and `None` when the probe itself failed (network/auth/timeout).
- **Remote-observed verdict before any failure report.** Before `finish` reports a push failure (`PushTimeoutError`, a process-group kill, or a non-zero `git push` exit that is not a non-fast-forward), every non-success outcome is routed through the probe — including the non-fast-forward retry push in `_recover_non_fast_forward_push()` — and the verification is time-bounded and uses only ref/object plumbing (it must not invoke the pre-push hook or the test suite).
- **Verified landed is success, not failure.** When verification confirms the commit is on `origin/dev`, `finish` completes normally: it records the completion comment naming the commit, performs the existing success-path cleanup (process cleanup, worktree removal, parent-branch sync), leaves the work item `completed`/`in_review` (terminal read-back still passes), and marks the report explicitly (`steps.push.verified_after_failure: true` plus the original error text) with an explanatory work-item comment.
- **Genuine failure and unknown outcome stay conservative.** When verification finds the commit absent from `origin/dev`, or verification itself fails (e.g. an `ls-remote` network error), `finish` still fails conservatively: the status resets to `open`, the manual-push/worktree recovery comment is posted, the worktree is retained, and the message/report distinguishes `push failed (commit not on origin/dev)` from `push outcome unknown (remote verification failed: <reason>)`, never claiming success without positive verification.
- **Ancestry, additive fields, preserved behaviour, no duplicate probe.** The commit is considered landed when it is an ancestor of the current `origin/dev` tip, never equality; the probe is extracted so the existing post-success ancestry assertion `_assert_commit_on_origin_dev()` (SA-0MVPZG7A0000N66U) reuses it instead of shipping a divergent second probe; non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry, worktree retention on genuine failure, the pre-push main-checkout mutation guard and `_sync_parent_branch` safe-skip semantics keep working; and `report["steps"]["push"]` keeps its existing `success`/`hash` keys (new keys are additive only).

## Goal

Make `phase_start` branch-aware so an existing child branch no longer fails
generically with "Failed to create worktree". The branch is either reused
(identical to / fast-forwardable from the parent branch) or the operator gets
an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the target child branch (`wl-<id>-<slug>`) already exists, `phase_start` no longer fails generically: it either reuses the existing worktree/branch (when that branch is at, or fast-forwardable from, the parent branch) or fails with an actionable error naming the stale branch and the recovery command.
- `git_worktree_add`'s boolean-only contract is extended so the caller can distinguish "branch exists" from other failures (`created` / `branch-exists` / `failed` verdicts), with the single `phase_start` call site updated and the source-order assertion in `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py` kept satisfied.
- Reuse path: a branch whose tip is an ancestor of (or equal to) the parent branch is fast-forwarded to the parent tip with `git branch -f` and registered with `git worktree add <path> <branch>` (no `-b`); the report sets `reused_branch: true` and `branch_fast_forwarded: true|false`.
- Unsafe path: a branch carrying commits not reachable from the parent branch (or from `origin/<parent_branch>`) is never reset or reused silently; `phase_start` fails with the branch name, the unique-commit count and the exact recovery commands, and resets the item to `open`.
- A branch checked out in another worktree is reported by name and never raced.
- The xfail markers added by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite" for this behaviour are removed and the tests pass.

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- Introduce verdict constants + `branch_exists(repo_root, branch)` (via
  `git show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>`) and
  `_branch_reuse_verdict(repo_root, branch, parent_branch)` returning
  `identical` / `fast-forwardable` / `unique-commits`, plus
  `_branch_checked_out_in_other_worktree(repo_root, branch)`.
- Change `git_worktree_add` to return the verdict string; keep the call
  prefix `git_worktree_add(branch,` so existing source-order assertions hold.
- In `phase_start` step 7, when `not resumed` and `branch_exists`: compute the
  verdict, fast-forward when safe, then register the worktree from the
  existing branch; otherwise set `report["success"] = False`,
  `report["stale_branch"] = {branch, unique_commits, recovery_commands}` and
  return after resetting status to `open`.
- Report the decision under `report["steps"]["worktree_branch"]` so `parent`
  and `drive` reports surface why a start reused a branch.

## Constraints

- Never `git branch -f`, `reset` or delete a branch that has commits absent
  from the parent branch — reuse is limited to branches with no unique
  commits.
- Do not weaken the main-checkout placement guard, stash-hygiene gate, code
  freeze gate, or parent-tracking assertion.
- Preserve `--worktree-path` override semantics and the idempotent worktree
  resume path (`_is_worktree`).
- Re-running `start` after a successful reuse must be idempotent (no second
  branch, no second worktree, no duplicate comment).

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_worktree_add`, new branch helpers, `phase_start` step 7
- `tests/test_implement_start_resume.py`
- `tests/test_implement_stale_branch.py` (added by the test-first child)
- `tests/test_implement_node_modules_symlink.py` (source-order assertion)

- Blocked by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite" (test-first).

## Deliverables

- Verdict-returning `git_worktree_add` plus branch state helpers.
- `phase_start` reuse / fast-forward / actionable-error behaviour.
- Green regression tests for the AC3 matrix.

# Implement safe branch cleanup

## Goal

Stop a failed or aborted `start` from poisoning the next `start` with a
orphaned feature branch: clean up the branch this run created, remove the
abandoned branch on `abort` when it is safe to do so, and always report what
was removed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `start` that fails after creating the branch cleans up the branch it created; `phase_abort` removes the abandoned feature branch (with a guarded delete — never force-deleting a branch with unmerged commits that are the only copy) and reports what it removed.
- The failed-`start` cleanup also removes the worktree registration it created, so no half-created `.worklog/worktrees/wl-*` directory survives the failure.
- `phase_abort` discovers the abandoned branch by prefix (`refs/heads/wl-<item-id>-*`) rather than needing the item title, deletes it with `git branch -d` semantics only when it has no unique commits, and reports `branch_removed` / `branch_retained` with the reason and the recovery command.
- A branch that carries commits not reachable from the parent branch or `origin/<parent_branch>` is retained and named in the abort report and comment — never force-deleted.
- The xfail markers added by "Test: Stale-branch recovery regression suite" for this behaviour are removed and the tests pass.
- The full project test suite passes with the new changes (enforced at the dev-push gate).

## Minimal Implementation (end-to-end slice)

- New `_delete_branch_if_safe(repo_root, branch, parent_branch)` returning
  `{deleted, reason, unique_commits}` with reasons `deleted` / `not-found` /
  `unique-commits` / `checked-out-elsewhere` / `error`; unique-commit count is
  taken against both the local parent branch and `origin/<parent_branch>`.
- New `_discover_item_branches(repo_root, work_item_id)` via
  `git for-each-ref --format=%(refname:short) "refs/heads/wl-<id>-*"`.
- Wrap the post-`git worktree add` steps of `phase_start` so a failure after
  creation removes the worktree (guarded by `_remove_worktree`) and then
  deletes the branch this run created, reporting
  `report["cleanup"] = {worktree_removed, branch_removed, reason}`.
- In `phase_abort`, after the worktree removal and before
  `_restore_repo_state`, delete each discovered item branch that is safe and
  record the outcome on the abort comment.

## Constraints

- No blind `git branch -D`: deletion is only reached when the unique-commit
  count is zero, and a branch checked out in another worktree is never
  touched.
- Cleanup failures are logged and reported, never fatal to `abort`.
- Idempotent: a second abort finds no branch and reports `not-found` without
  error.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_delete_branch_if_safe`, `_discover_item_branches`, `phase_start` post-create failure path, `phase_abort`

- Failed-start cleanup of the worktree and the branch it created.

# Release gate: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit-stage bound

## Goal (user story)

As a producer running a release (`/skill:ship release`) on a contended host, I want the release
gate to distinguish "the suite is red" from "the host is busy", so a busy machine can no longer
fail a green release with a 300 s hang timeout. The unit stage, not a browser loop, was the abort
point this time — the diagnostic currently explains only browser-stage hangs and conflates elapsed
time with the bound.

## Background (discovered in CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09, superseded — see Appendix)

The dev→main release gate aborted the TCE v0.1.24 release with
`[hang-timeout] Vitest run did not complete within 300s — aborting (exit 124)` +
`[vitest-runner] attempts=1 status=124 outcome=hang args="--project unit" expected=241 ran=indeterminate`.
No test failed — the unit stage was still working through 241 files under host load (three
concurrent suite runs + a Monte-Carlo sweep; 16 cores, load average reported 35–42). A retry cost
a full 20+ minute re-run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `[hang-timeout]` abort reports, in the same message: the aborted stage (
  `--project unit` / `--project browser` / the pre-flight `vitest list`), the configured bound,
  the elapsed wall time, the delta over the bound, and the host load average at abort plus the
  core count — so contention is distinguishable from a genuine hang without opening the cache entry.
- The hang diagnostic's guidance is stage-appropriate: the browser-stage paragraph (starved
  `requestAnimationFrame`, undestroyed `Phaser.Game`, run one file under `--project browser`) is
  **not** printed for a unit-stage abort, which instead points at a synchronous loop in
  test/engine code.
- The unit-stage wall-clock bound adopts the operator-approved **hybrid** strategy: a raised
  **static floor** (justified against the measured baseline — TCE green unit stages observed at
  88–217 s against the current 300 s bound, i.e. ~1.4× headroom) **plus load-aware scaling** of the
  bound from the sampled 1-min load average relative to the core count, **up to a finite ceiling**;
  the bound remains overridable per host (`--timeout-ms`).
- The hybrid bound's rationale and the measured baseline are recorded in the runner/CI header
  comment(s) and in the release-gate documentation (this repo's `docs/`, and TCE's
  `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh` header + `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Hang timeout).
- Inner stage bounds stay consistent with the outer gate budget: the sum of stage bounds cannot
  silently exceed the outer per-command timeout (TCE `.pi/test-config.json` →
  `timeoutPerCommand: 1500`, for an 18–21 min suite — ~4–7 min headroom), so raising/scaling an
  inner bound either adjusts the outer budget in the same change or documents why it still fits.
- Hang semantics are unchanged: exit `124` (`HANG_TIMEOUT_EXIT_CODE`), hangs are **never
  retried**, and the `--expect-project-coverage` gate still fails closed on an incomplete run.
- Tests cover the new diagnostic content (stage, bound, elapsed, delta, load average) and the
  bound/load behaviour deterministically: the load average is injected through a test seam and is
  never read from the real host.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README,
  and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A producer can retry a release on a busy machine and see immediately whether the suite or the host
was at fault, instead of losing a full-suite run to a timeout that had nothing to do with the code.

## Constraints

- **Do not weaken hang detection.** Exit 124, "hangs are never retried" and the fail-closed
  coverage gate are invariants (TCE precedent CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N, CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H); a bound
  that never fires is a regression in the opposite direction — keep the ceiling finite and print
  the bound in the diagnostic so an operator can see how generous it was.
- **Portability.** The bound must remain an explicit, per-host tunable; a load-aware bound is an
  addition, not a replacement for an overridable number, and smaller CI hosts still get a sane
  floor.
- **Determinism in tests.** Never read the real load average in a test; sample it behind an
  injectable seam.
- **Cross-repo tracking.** This item owns the work; TCE-side files below are edited in the TCE
  checkout (per the cross-repo convention) and recorded on this item. The release gate itself
  lives in `skill/ship/` in this repo.
- **Scope discipline.** A fully load-aware *outer* gate timeout and per-file retry budgets are out
  of scope; record them as linked work items rather than folding them in.

## Key Files (predicted)

- This repo (framework): `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (outer per-command timeout budgeting,
  any stage-bound surface), `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` (gate log surface),
  release-gate docs in `docs/`.
- Cross-repo (TCE checkout; tracked here): `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` (hang diagnostic
  content, load-average sampling seam, hybrid bound derivation), `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  (unit-stage `--timeout-ms 300000`, header comment rationale),
  `tests/scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.test.ts` (diagnostic + bound coverage with injected load),
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` (hang-timeout section ~line 1313, test-config section ~line 816),
  `.pi/test-config.json` (`timeoutPerCommand: 1500` if the outer budget is adjusted).

## Design decision for the plan (not blocking intake)

The hybrid bound may be implemented **in place** in TCE's `scripts/vitest-run-with-retry.ts` with
this item tracking the change, or the bounded runner may be **lifted into the framework**
(e.g. under `skill/test/scripts/`) and consumed by TCE. Both satisfy the ACs; the plan decides and
records the choice, keeping the diagnostic and bound computation in exactly one place.

## Related work

- **CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N** (TCE, completed) — introduced the bounded wall-clock abort, exit 124,
  the never-retry rule, and raised the browser bound 15→20 min after variance straddled the old
  limit; this item is the same failure mode one stage earlier.
- **CG-0MVL21CVM003VK5H** (TCE, completed) — the project-coverage gate whose fail-closed behaviour
  must be preserved.
- **CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09** (TCE, superseded/deleted) — the original intake that produced this
  brief; measured evidence and the evidence corrections (retry log shows a producer-review block,
  not a green retry; load 35–42 is an observation, not a log) carry over.
- **SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81** (this repo) — the full-suite-at-dev-push gate design this work hardens.
- Sibling item: **the green-cache-entry resume path** (created alongside this one) — keeps a
  unit-stage abort from forcing a full re-run of an unchanged tree.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (bound strategy: A static raise / B load-aware only / C hybrid) — ANSWERED: C (hybrid).**
  Asked 2026-11-13 by Map in intake on CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09; answered by producer (comment on that
  item): "1. C". Agent recommendation (adopted): C. Research: TCE `scripts/run-ci-tests.sh`
  bounds at lines 56/92/96; `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand: 1500` and
  `docs/DEVELOPER.md` line 816 ("full suite takes 18–21 minutes"); measured green TCE unit stages
  from `.worklog/cache/*/stdout.txt` — 88, 96, 106, 111, 128, 141, 147, 149, 206, 217 s (worst
  217 s on 2026-11-11 17:37); no load-average awareness exists anywhere in TCE `scripts/` today.
- **Q2 (resume-path scope) — ANSWERED: B (split; framework item).** Answered by producer: "2. B".
  Tracked in the sibling item created alongside this one.
- **Duplicate check** — searched `wl search "hang timeout vitest retry"` (TCE) and this repo's
  items: the browser-stage precedent (CG-0MT08R2QR0070F3N) is completed and does not cover the
  unit-stage bound, the diagnostics content, or the resume path; no duplicate found.

within the cache TTL instead of re-executing the whole suite.

## Background (discovered in CG-0MWE9E8IP0010D09, superseded — see Appendix)

The TCE v0.1.24 release gate aborted in the unit stage with a 300 s hang bound (exit 124; no
failing test — host contention, load 35–42 on 16 cores). The per-repo test cache is keyed on
command + git state with a 2 h TTL; the hang **overwrites** the cache entry for that state with
`exit_code: 124`, so a retry on the same tree re-runs every stage from scratch. The release gate
runs `python3 run_tests.py --scope full --strict-git-env` on the merged dev→main tree.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A hang/abort result (exit `124` from the bounded vitest runner, or any non-zero abort that
  produced no parsable test results) does **not** destroy a green cache entry for the same tree
  state: when a valid green entry exists for the requested command+state within TTL, the cached
  green verdict is served even if a later aborted run wrote to the same key, and the abort is
  still reported (the gate must never *silently* accept an abort as green).
- The resume path is functional end-to-end: re-running the release gate against an unchanged tree
  (same git state, within TTL) after a unit-stage abort consumes the preserved green full-suite
  entry instead of re-executing `npm --silent test`, with the cache TTL gate intact.
- The release gate documents the resume procedure: `run_tests.py`/cache behaviour and the
  operator-visible statement ("the tree is unchanged within TTL — re-run resumes green") are
  described in this repo's release-gate docs and in `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`
  comments; no green-entry destruction happens on abort.
- A failure or changed tree still executes and stores freshly — the preservation never masks a red
  run, a changed git state, or an expired TTL: cache behaviour for abort entries is covered by
  tests in this repo (`tests/` alongside `test_cache.py` / `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README,
  and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A contended-host abort stops costing a full re-run: the producer retries the release and the gate
resumes from the green entry for the unchanged tree, holding the green verdict while the abort is
still surfaced.

## Constraints

- **Never mask a genuine failure.** A preserved green entry is served only for the same command +
  git state within TTL; any tree change, red verdict, or TTL expiry forces a fresh run.
- **Green-first, but loud.** Returning the preserved green entry must be paired with a clear
  notice that the *aborted* run is being satisfied from the earlier green entry (operator
  visibility), not a silent acceptance of exit 124.
- **Follow the existing cache contract.** Keying, git-state fingerprinting, `scope` / `test_type`
  namespacing and the state-changed quarantine in `test_cache.py` are unchanged; this item only
  refines what a hang/abort writes.
- **Cross-repo consumers.** TCE's audit/release flows consume `query_cached()`; their
  expectations (read-only, verdicts only for matching state) must not regress.

## Key Files (predicted)

  green-entry preservation; TTL unchanged.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — `run_cached`/`query_cached` usage, abort-result reporting.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — full-suite gate (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81),

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `query_cached` consumer; must still reject partial/abort

- `tests/` — coverage for abort-vs-green preservation in this repo's test suite.
- Cross-repo (TCE, tracked here): `docs/DEVELOPER.md` § Hang timeout / § Test Configuration —
  document the resume path for TCE release operators.

## Related work

- **Sibling item: stage-aware hang diagnostics + hybrid load-aware unit bound** (created alongside

  recover from. These are complementary, not sequential.

# `implement.py start` must not fork a worktree from a local parent branch that is behind `origin/<parent>`

Mirror of the AI_Hell discovery report **AH-0MWFF40700014EE2** (`discovered-from:AH-0MWFF40700014EE2`).
Per the precedent producer decision for **SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1 ← AH-0MUD8QNRG006MCKB**
(2026-09-25: "the fix and regression tests live in the SorraAgents counterpart; no
implementation change is required in AI_Hell"), the actionable fix lives here, where
`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` is.

## Problem

`implement.py start` refreshes the local parent branch before `git worktree add`, but
`_sync_parent_branch` **skips** the refresh when the local `dev` ref is diverged or cannot
be fetched non-checked-out (`reason: "diverged_or_checked_out"`), and `phase_start` then
forks the worktree from that stale local `dev` anyway (`git_worktree_add(branch,
abs_wt_path, parent_branch)` → `git worktree add --track -b <branch> <wt> dev`). The child
session inherits a base missing commits already published on `origin/dev`.

Observed during AH-0MWF0CS4I001XZHU (driven child of AH-0MVWZYIWX0008C55):

- the main checkout's `dev` was `ahead 1, behind 8` of `origin/dev` (`e38797b8` local-only,
  duplicating `9687a6db`'s content);
- the worktree forked at `e38797b8`, so its changed-scope test gate ran an unrelated
  `scripts/capture-scenes.test.ts` against pre-fix source and went **red** on a failure
  `origin/dev` had already fixed (`HANGAR_WAR_SCENE_KEYS` still listing the deleted
  `DefenceReportScene`);
- the session had to rebase onto `origin/dev` (`8d1c1aca`) by hand before it could pass its
  gate and push.

The same symptom is recorded in AH-0MWEYVRUX008SLJ8's completion comments ("Push to dev
initially failed (non-fast-forward …). Rebased onto origin/dev and retried"), so this is
recurring, not a one-off.

## Expected behaviour

A worktree forked by `start` is based on a ref whose commits are all contained in
`origin/<parent>` (a fast-forward ancestor of `origin/<parent>`), so a driven child never
starts behind the published base.

## Approach (decided)

The AI_Hell report listed two candidate approaches ("fork from `origin/<parent>`" or
"warn loudly"); the acceptance criteria pin the first and make the second mandatory
reporting, so both are in scope:

1. `_sync_parent_branch` reports `ahead`/`behind` counts (via
   `git rev-list --left-right --count <local>...refs/remotes/origin/<parent>`) on every
   skip reason where the counts are computable, in addition to `reason`/`warning`.
2. A new resolver decides the fork base: **fork from
   `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` whenever the local parent is behind `origin/<parent>`
   (`behind > 0`, which includes the diverged case); otherwise keep the current local-branch
   base.** The local ref is never force-updated — a diverged local `dev` stays exactly as it
   is for the operator to reconcile.
3. `phase_start` records the choice: `report["steps"]["worktree_base"] = {ref, reason,
   ahead, behind}` and an extended "Implementation started"/"resumed" comment naming the base
   ref and, when the local branch was skipped, why plus the ahead/behind counts.
4. Fail-open is preserved: a held main-checkout lock, a failed fetch, or a dirty main checkout
   never blocks `start`; when the counts cannot be computed (fetch failed / no remote-tracking
   ref) the local branch remains the base exactly as today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — `implement.py start` never forks a worktree from a local parent branch that is
  behind `origin/<parent>`: either the local ref is fast-forwarded or the worktree is forked
  from `origin/<parent>`.
- **AC2** — The start report/comment names the base ref used and, when the local parent branch
  was skipped (diverged / checked out / lock held), states why and the ahead/behind counts.
- **AC3** — A driven child started from a diverged local `dev` passes its first changed-scope
  gate without a manual rebase (regression test with a synthetic diverged local branch).
- **AC4** — Existing behaviour is preserved: a lock-held or fetch-failed refresh still fails
  open (never blocks `start`) and never force-updates a diverged branch.

## Implementation sketch

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
  - `_sync_parent_branch` (~line 7456): add `ahead`/`behind` to the skipped results
    (`diverged`, `diverged_or_checked_out`, and the other safe-skip paths where computable).
  - New `_resolve_worktree_base_ref(repo_root, parent_branch, refresh_result) -> dict`:
    returns `{"ref", "reason", "ahead", "behind", "skipped_local"}`; picks
    `refs/remotes/origin/<parent>` when behind > 0.
  - `phase_start` Step 7 (~line 11370): pass the resolved ref to `git_worktree_add`, record
    `report["steps"]["worktree_base"]`, and name it in the start/resume comment (~line 11431).
  - `git_worktree_add` (~line 3435): document that the base may be a fully-qualified
    remote-tracking ref; assert the new branch still tracks `origin/<parent>` (the
    `--track` upstream must not change — `finish` pushes to `origin/dev`).
- Tests (test-first, new file `skill/implement/tests/test_phase_start_base_ref.py`, following
  the hermetic-fixture patterns in `test_phase_start_resume_from_worktree.py` /
  `test_phase_start_claim.py`).
- Docs: `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` (start section ~2204-2216, ~4029) and
  `skill/implement/SKILL.md` (~357) — document the base-ref resolution and the new report
  keys/skip reasons.

## Related work

- `discovered-from:AH-0MWFF40700014EE2` (AI_Hell discovery report; counterpart of this item)
- SA-0MUGX1DIT000M7S1 (completed) — `finish` now fast-forwards local `dev` after the push;
  that closes the *common* stale-local-dev case, leaving the diverged/lock-held skip this
  item fixes.
- SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO — main-checkout lock shared by `start`'s refresh and `finish`.
- SA-0MVXUGXS5006M3HF — `start` resume-from-worktree path resolved against the main checkout.
- SA-0MVRN5Q67005H3M5 — behind-only child worktree detection (same "stale base" family).

## Impact

Driven child sessions start from the published base, so they stop burning a rebase and a red
gate on work someone else already shipped.

# Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6)

## Problem statement

Implement sessions that run concurrently spend the overwhelming majority of their
wall-clock waiting on a single per-repository `flock`, because `implement.py finish`
holds that lock across its **whole** commit → fast-forward → push → post-push window
and the dev-push **pre-push hook runs the full test suite (~5.4 min)** inside it.
Every concurrent `finish` therefore serialises its expensive test run behind the
others. At the intended fan-out of **up to 6 concurrent sessions**, the sixth finish
queues behind five ~5-min full-suite runs.

## Evidence (2026-11-13, AI_Hell implement-skill sessions)

Analysed the 36 worktree sessions that started with the implement skill
(`~/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell-.worklog-*`):

- **668 min** summed session time over a **388 min (6.5 h)** wall-clock span —
  only **1.7x effective parallelism** at a **peak measured concurrency of 4**.
- **88–93%** of each long session's wall-clock was inside `bash` tool calls
  (waiting on processes), not model reasoning or edits.
- Time buckets: **wait_for_job 249 min (37%)** (215.9 min of it lock-waits),
  own `finish` 133 min (20%), scoped tests 57 min (9%), hand-rolled
  `sleep`/`grep` polling loops 48 min (7%).
- **57** "another run holds the repository lock" refusals; **46** observed
  lock-waits averaging **4.3 min** (median 5 min, **max 21.5 min**). Worst single
  tool call: **45 min** = a `for attempt in 1..8` retry loop absorbing five
  consecutive lock holders.
- **21** non-fast-forward rebase events, each creating a new tree that re-triggers
  the full-suite pre-push gate (9 full-suite gate runs today).
- 9 sessions were **no-ops** (3 messages, ~50 s) — drive retries that immediately
  gave up.

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch of up to 6 concurrent implement sessions
  (the intended operating point) on a single repository.
- **Implement-skill sessions** (leaf and driven child) whose `finish` currently queues
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs.
- **Producers/reviewers** who need the speed-up evidenced, not asserted.

User stories:

- As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
  complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised queueing
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in roughly the
  time of one work item rather than the sum of all of them.
- As a driven child session, I want my single `finish` call to wait boundedly on the
  lock instead of scripting retry loops.
- As a producer, I want a recorded before/after measurement before the epic is closed.

## Goal

As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised
queueing behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in
roughly the time of one work item rather than the sum of all of them.

## Decomposition

The epic is decomposed into five child items; together they own every acceptance
criterion below.

1. Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock
   (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — the single biggest time sink: stop holding the exclusive
   repository lock across the ~5.4 min full-suite gate.
2. Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops

# Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1). This is the single biggest time sink identified in the
2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis.

## Problem statement

`implement.py finish` acquires the per-repository `flock`
(`<main-checkout>/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock`) at Step 3c and holds it until
the `finally` block — covering commit → fast-forward local dev → **push** → post-push
verification. The dev push triggers `.githooks/pre-push`, which runs the **full test
suite** (`run_tests.py --scope full`, measured ~326 s / 5.4 min for AI_Hell) while the
lock is held. A read-only test run is therefore made part of the exclusive mutating
critical section, so every concurrent `finish` serialises its ~5-min suite behind the
others. This is the root cause of the 37% `wait_for_job` share and the 46 lock-waits
(median 5 min, max 21.5 min).

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch of up to 6 concurrent implement sessions.
- **Implement-skill session** whose `finish` currently spends most of its wall-clock
  waiting for the lock rather than doing work.

User stories:

- As an operator running a 6-way fan-out, I want concurrent finishes to overlap their
  full-suite gate runs so the batch finishes in roughly the time of one work item
  rather than the sum of all of them.
- As an implement-skill session, I want the exclusive repository lock to cover only
  the short mutating window, so my `finish` is not blocked for another session's
  ~5-minute test run.

## Goal

As an operator running concurrent implement sessions, I want the full-suite gate to
run **without** holding the exclusive repository lock, so concurrent finishes overlap
their test time instead of queueing on it.

## Approach

- Resolve the full-suite verdict for the *pushed tree* **before** taking the
  main-checkout lock (the tree-keyed cache already exists — reuse it), or run the
  suite under only the shared `test` semaphore lane, not the repo lock.
- Keep the lock covering only the true mutations: commit → fast-forward → push →
  ancestry assertion (should be seconds).
- Preserve the existing safety invariants: single-owner mutation of the shared `dev`
  ref, the bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, and the tree/provenance binding of
  the verdict (no verdict about a different tree may be trusted).

## Acceptance criteria

- The full test suite is never executed while `main-checkout.lock` is held (asserted
  by a test that observes lock state across the suite invocation).
- The lock-hold window in a green `finish` is bounded and does not include the
  full-suite duration (measured/asserted in a test or documented metric).
- A concurrent-finish integration test shows the second finish's wait is materially
  shorter when the first is running the full suite (no longer serialised on suite
  time).
- No regression in the existing finish-concurrency / ancestry-assertion tests.
- At least one automated test proves the new gate/lock ordering (lock state observed
  while the suite runs, and a green finish whose lock window excludes the suite).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The shared `dev` ref stays single-owner: exactly one finish mutates it at a time and
  the ancestry assertion after the push is unchanged.
- The gate verdict remains provenance-bound and tree-keyed (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV,
  SA-0MVQHVHXI007PQAB): no verdict about a different tree may be reused, and a
  rebased commit legitimately produces a new tree (see the sibling rebase item).
- The bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` behaviour is preserved — no unbounded
  lock hold.
- Out of scope: trimming the full suite's own runtime, sharding, per-file caching,
  raising `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` (per-project concerns), and changing changed-scope
  test selection.

## Existing state

- `phase_finish` acquires `main-checkout.lock` at Step 3c and holds it through push
  and post-push verification.
- `.githooks/pre-push` always runs `run_tests.py --scope full` for pushes to
  `dev`/`main` (scope-aware gate, SA-0MT6CEN8D0073F61) and is bound to the pushed
  commit (`--gate-commit`), with a tree-keyed verdict cache and cache mirroring into
  the main checkout.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` already allocates an independent `test` semaphore
  lane and caches verdicts with `fingerprint_kind="tree"`.

## Desired change

The expensive read-only suite runs outside the exclusive repository lock (either
before acquiring it, keyed on the would-be pushed tree, or under the `test` lane
only), and the lock window shrinks to the commit → fast-forward → push → ancestry
assertion sequence.

## Impact

Concurrent finishes stop serialising behind each other's full-suite runs, so an
operator's 6-way fan-out batch completes in roughly the time of a single work item
instead of queueing six ~5-minute suites one after another.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 3c lock acquisition and the push/gate window (search `Step 3c`, `acquire_main_checkout_lock`)
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — full-suite gate entry point, `test` semaphore lane, tree-keyed verdict cache (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`)
- `.githooks/pre-push` — dev/main full-suite gate that today runs inside the lock window
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — `RepoLock` / `release_repo_lock` implementing `main-checkout.lock`
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` — existing lock-window tests to extend
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish lock/timeout documentation to update

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — lock helper reused here.
- implement.py finish: concurrent sessions orphan each other's commits via the shared local-dev fast-forward (SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY) — establishes the single-owner lock invariant.
- Hermetic regression tests for finish concurrency orphans (SA-0MVPZG01J0067PC2) — test patterns to reuse.
- Defer full suite to dev-push (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) — why the full suite is at the gate at all.
- Tree-keyed gate verdict (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV) — the cache this item must reuse.
- Sibling items: Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops (SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF); Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC).
- Session-time analysis skill (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) — feeds the epic-level before/after measurement.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** making the suite asynchronous (background gate) would weaken
  the "never push an unverified tree" guarantee — out of scope; the verdict must still
  gate the push.
- **Risk:** moving the suite before the lock could test a tree that is then invalidated
  by a rebase; mitigations: reuse the tree-keyed verdict, and treat a rebase-produced
  tree as a cache miss (handled by the sibling rebase item).
- **Assumption:** the `dev` push gate stays `scope=full` for release-critical refs.
- **Assumption:** the suite's own runtime is a per-project concern; only the serialising
  effect is addressed here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence base: the
2026-11-13 AI_Hell 36-session analysis recorded on the parent epic
(SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1 comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR), plus operator decisions recorded
there (concurrency target up to 6; per-project full-suite trimming out of scope).
Researched directly in the repository: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
(Step 3c lock window), `.githooks/pre-push` (full-suite gate), and
`skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` (tree-keyed verdict cache).

# Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).

## Problem statement

`IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` defaults to 0 (fail fast). When the lock is held, the
agent must re-enter the queue itself, so the skill guidance teaches a hand-rolled
`for attempt in 1..8; implement.py finish ... ; wait_for_job.py --pid <holder> ...`
loop. In the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis this pattern produced the single worst tool
call — **45 minutes** absorbing five consecutive lock holders — and accounted for a
large share of the 37% `wait_for_job` time plus 48 min (7%) of separate `sleep`/`grep`
polling loops. Each fail-fast refusal is also a wasted model round-trip.

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch: wants predictable, minimal waiting per session.
- **Implement-skill session** that currently has to script retry loops around
  `implement.py finish`.

User stories:

- As an implement-skill session, I want one `finish` call to wait internally on the
  lock (bounded, with progress) so I do not burn model round-trips on retry loops.
- As an operator watching a batch, I want a waiting session to report who holds the
  lock and to fail with an actionable message only when the bound expires.

## Goal

As an operator, I want a waiting `finish` to perform **one** bounded internal wait on
the flock (with progress), instead of the agent scripting fail-fast retry loops around
it, so concurrent finishes do not multiply round-trips and confusing logs.

## Approach

- Make a positive bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` the guidance default (or
  document setting it) so `finish` waits internally on the flock up to a generous
  bound, emitting progress.
- Remove the `for attempt in ... ; implement.py finish ... ; wait_for_job` retry-loop
  guidance from the implement skill; replace with the single bounded-wait instruction.
- Ensure the internal wait reports the holder and honours `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` cleanly.

## Acceptance criteria

- `implement.py finish` with a positive `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` waits on the
  lock internally within the bound, reporting the holder, and fails with an
  actionable message only when the bound expires.
- The implement skill docs contain no bespoke finish retry-loop pattern; they instruct
  a single bounded wait.
- A waiting `finish` performs **one** bounded internal wait rather than N fail-fast round-trips, and the skill guidance contains no bespoke `for attempt ...; wait_for_job` finish retry loops.
- A test covers: lock held → `finish` waits → holder releases → `finish` proceeds
  (no fail-fast refusal).
- Regression test that the wait is bounded (never hangs) and is signal-safe.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The wait must stay bounded: a configured timeout always terminates the wait with an
  actionable refusal naming the holder and the lock path.
- `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` must release the held lock and the child lock and exit cleanly
  (no orphaned locks).
- Default behaviour must stay safe for unattended sessions: a positive bound must not
  be able to wedge a batch indefinitely.
- Out of scope: changing the single-owner lock semantics or removing the lock.

## Existing state

- `DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT = 0.0` (fail fast), env `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`,
  read by `_finish_lock_timeout()`; the bounded wait lives in
  `shared.repo_lock.RepoLock` via `acquire_main_checkout_lock`.
- The implement skill documents the current fail-fast behaviour, and sessions work
  around it with `for attempt ... ; wait_for_job.py --pid <holder>` loops.
- Lock holders are recorded with pid/host metadata, so the holder can already be named
  in a refusal.

## Desired change

`finish` performs one bounded internal wait with progress and holder reporting; the
skill guidance describes that single call instead of a bespoke retry loop.

## Impact

An operator's concurrent batch stops multiplying model round-trips and multi-minute
tool calls on lock contention: a waiting session reports who holds the lock and
proceeds automatically once released.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `ENV_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `_finish_lock_timeout()`, `acquire_main_checkout_lock` call in `phase_finish`
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — bounded wait implementation and holder reporting
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — guidance that must lose the bespoke retry-loop pattern
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` and `skill/implement/tests/test_lock_timeout_isolation.py` — test homes for the wait behaviour
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — timeout documentation

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — the lock/wait helper.
- implement test suite inherits IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT from the ambient environment and hangs for hours (SA-0MVY0G5EH000LIMB) — timeout inheritance hazard to keep in mind.
- Sibling item: Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — the other half of lock-wait reduction.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** building a general-purpose lock queue service is out of scope;
  this item is one bounded wait inside `finish`.
- **Risk:** a long default bound could make an unattended batch appear hung; mitigation:
  progress output plus a clear expiry message, and the default chosen deliberately
  (documented) rather than "infinite".
- **Assumption:** the holder pid/identity metadata recorded by `RepoLock` is sufficient
  to name the holder in progress output.
- **Assumption:** removing the retry-loop guidance from the skill does not break driven
  sessions, which call `finish` once per child.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence base: 2026-11-13 AI_Hell
36-session analysis on the parent epic (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1, comment
SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR), including the 45-minute worst-case tool call and the 48 min of
`sleep`/`grep` polling. Researched in the repository: `_finish_lock_timeout()` /
`DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` and the bounded
wait in `skill/shared/repo_lock.py`.

The epic's lock-contention target is evidenced by a repeatable, recorded before/after
analysis, and any shortfall becomes visible follow-up work instead of an assumption.

The operator can see, in recorded numbers, whether a 6-way fan-out now completes in
roughly the time of one work item — instead of trusting that the fixes helped.
